This chart compares countries on two development-related measures: learning-adjusted years of schooling and the Electoral Democracy Index.
The source context identifies this as an Our World in Data chart using education data from the World Bank methodology and democracy data from V-Dem.
Learning-adjusted years of schooling combines time spent in school with the quality of learning achieved, so it is intended to reflect not just attendance but effective educational attainment.
The Electoral Democracy Index ranges from 0 to 1, where higher values indicate more democratic electoral institutions.
Because the education measure is learning-adjusted, two countries with similar years in school can still differ if students learn different amounts.
If a country has many years of schooling but weak learning outcomes, the learning-adjusted measure can reveal that formal access to school is not translating into equivalent human capital.
